personnelNotes: One surname is printed three ways across the charter: Maria Francia Celedonio, Ma. Francia Celedonio and Maria Francia Celdonio. The fullest spelling is used here.
The charter also credits unnamed job order workers on the vaccination and dog catching services.

feedbackMechanism.howToSendFeedback: Raise feedback or a complaint with the City Veterinary Office.

services.title: Bringing an animal in for treatment
services.description: Treatment for a sick animal brought to the City Veterinary Office. The vet assesses the animal, gives the treatment or medication, signs the health card and issues a prescription if one is needed.

steps.client: Bring the animal in for treatment.
steps.agency: Records the client and patient information.

steps.client: State your concern and give the necessary information about the animal.
steps.agency: Prepares the animal health card or certificate of registration.
Assesses the animal's condition, recommends treatment or medication, and administers the procedure.
Signs the animal health card or certificate of registration and issues a prescription if needed.

verifyNotes: This charter prints no TOTAL row for any of its services, so every total shown is summed from the steps alone.

The charter runs in-patient and out-patient treatment under one heading, Veterinary Therapeutic Services, with the client steps restarting at 1 for the out-patient case. They are split here into two services sharing charter number 1, because you know before you come whether you are bringing the animal in or asking for a visit.
Every duration in this charter is a range. The arithmetic reads the upper figure of a range, so the derived totals are the longer end.

services.title: Asking for a farm or home visit
services.description: A visit from the office to diagnose and treat an animal where it is, with follow-up visits if they are needed. The times the charter gives exclude travel.

requirements.item: Request form containing the animal information and the owner's profile

steps.client: Fill up the request form with the animal information and your profile.
steps.agency: Interviews you and refers you to the livestock inspector or technician in charge.

steps.client: State your concern so possible treatment can be assessed.
steps.agency: Visits and diagnoses the patient, and gives the necessary medication.
Visits the patient again for follow-up treatment or medication, if needed.

notes: The charter's times exclude travel, so the visit itself takes longer than the figure shown.
verifyNotes: Split from the charter's combined therapeutic services block; see the note on bringing an animal in.
The charter prints no TOTAL row, so the total shown is summed from the steps alone. It also excludes travel time explicitly, so the derived total is not the time you should plan for.

services.title: Getting a veterinary health certificate to travel with a pet
services.description: The health certificate and shipping permit needed to transport an animal, as required by the Bureau of Animal Industry. If the animal's vaccination is not up to date the office vaccinates it first.

steps.client: Fill up the veterinary certificate request form.
steps.agency: Interviews you about the date and destination of the animal to be transported.
Verifies the vaccination records against the animal health card or vaccination certificate.

steps.client: Present the pet or animal for examination.
steps.agency: Conducts a physical examination of the animal.

steps.client: Go to the City Treasurer's Office to pay.
steps.agency: If approved, issues the referral slip for payment at the City Treasurer's Office. If not approved, carries out the applicable vaccination first.

steps.client: Present proof of payment to the clinic attendant.
steps.agency: Records the proof of payment issued by the City Treasurer's Office and gathers the client and animal information.
Prepares the shipping permit.
Reviews and signs the shipping permit.

steps.client: Sign the receiving logbook or file copy, and receive the veterinary health certificate.
steps.agency: Releases the shipping permit, to be received by the requesting party on signing the logbook or file copy.

notes: If the animal's vaccinations are not current, the office vaccinates it before approving the certificate.
verifyNotes: The charter prints no TOTAL row, so the total shown is summed from the steps alone.
Every duration is a range and the arithmetic reads the upper figure, so the derived total is the longer end.

services.title: Breeding, artificial insemination and livestock advice
services.description: Help with animal propagation: breeding, artificial insemination, and technical advice. A livestock technician evaluates the animal's breed and suitability first.

steps.client: Fill up the request slip for animal propagation assistance, whether breeding, artificial insemination, or technical advice.
steps.agency: Collects the data on the client and the animal concerned.
Assesses the client and refers them to the City Veterinarian.
Evaluates the animal based on the information provided.
Assigns a livestock inspector or technician to evaluate the animal's breed and suitability.

steps.client: Have the service carried out.
steps.agency: Where applicable, facilitates the artificial insemination or breeding service.
steps.feeText: Varies, according to the price of the semen

notes: The only charge is for the semen itself, and the charter does not publish a figure because it varies.
verifyNotes: The charter prints no TOTAL row, so the total shown is summed from the steps alone.

services.title: Barangay pre-registration of dogs and cats
services.description: How a barangay submits its survey of the dog and cat population so a rabies mass vaccination can be scheduled for it. This is a barangay-side service, not one an individual pet owner files.
services.whoMayAvail: Barangay Responsible Owners of Dog Enforcement Team (BRODET)

requirements.item: Canine and feline pre-registration form, 1 original copy
Canine and feline registration form, 1 original copy
Receipt summary issued by the barangay, 1 original copy
Official receipt of the barangay remittance on pet registration, 1 photocopy

steps.client: The barangay submits the pre-registration survey of its dog and cat population for vaccination.
steps.agency: Receives and reviews the documents submitted and determines the total number of dogs and cats surveyed and registered.
steps.processingTime: 5-8 minutes (varies with the volume of documents submitted)

steps.agency: Schedules the rabies mass vaccination.
Prepares the letter to the Barangay Captain giving the schedule of the mass vaccination.
Reviews and signs the communication letter.

steps.client: The barangay receives the letter.
steps.agency: Delivers the letter to the barangay concerned.

verifyNotes: The charter prints no TOTAL row, so the total shown is summed from the steps alone.
The first step's duration is explicitly said to vary with how many documents the barangay submits, so the figure shown is for a typical batch.

services.title: Rabies mass vaccination
services.description: The free house-to-house rabies vaccination run in each barangay once its pre-registration is in. Your pet is interviewed for, vaccinated, and the vaccination card filled up on the spot.

requirements.item: Canine and feline registration form submitted by the barangay
Receipt issued by the barangay, 1 photocopy

steps.client: Prepare your animals for vaccination.
steps.agency: Orients the barangay officials, barangay nutrition scholars and barangay tanod on the assistance needed for the mass vaccination.
Conducts the house-to-house vaccination.
steps.processingTime: Depends upon the distance between pet owners

steps.client: Present the vaccination card.
steps.agency: Interviews the owner or handler about the animal's current medical condition before vaccinating.
steps.personResponsible: Administrative Aide II / Administrative Aide I

steps.agency: Vaccinates the animals.
Fills up the vaccination cards.
Prepares and records the vaccination report.
Reviews and signs the pet registration of the vaccinated dogs and cats.

steps.client: The barangay receives its file copy.
steps.agency: Issues the vaccination summary and the certificate of registration, signed by the veterinarian and the vaccinator, as the barangay's file copy.

notes: The vaccination is free and comes to you: the team goes house to house once your barangay is scheduled.
verifyNotes: The charter prints no TOTAL row, so the total shown is summed from the steps alone.

Several durations are per pet or per dog rather than per visit, and the house-to-house step has no figure at all because it depends on distance. The derived total is therefore not the time one owner waits; it is closer to the office's own per-animal effort.

services.title: Reporting stray dogs and cats
services.description: How a barangay asks for help catching stray dogs and cats, what happens to the animals afterwards, and how an owner claims one back. Impounded animals are held at the barangay for three days, then moved to the city facility at Banquerohan.

requirements.item: Written request from the barangay to assist with dog catching activities, 1 original copy

steps.client: Report stray dogs to the barangay officials or the City Veterinary Office.
steps.agency: Receives the letter submitted by the requesting barangay.

steps.client: The barangay submits a written request for a dog catching activity.
steps.agency: Records the request.

steps.client: The barangay officials fill up the request form at the information desk.
steps.agency: Issues the request form or slip.

steps.client: The stray animal activity is carried out.
steps.agency: Coordinates with the barangay concerned to provide assistance on their dog catching activity.
steps.personResponsible: Administrative Aide IV and job order workers

steps.client: Impounded animals are temporarily housed at the barangay impounding facility for three days.
Citation tickets are issued to the identified owners.
To claim an impounded animal, settle the payment at the City Treasurer's Office.
steps.agency: Picks up the unclaimed impounded animals to be transferred to the temporary impounding facility in Banquerohan, Legazpi City, and shelters them.
steps.feeText: Settled at the City Treasurer's Office; the charter publishes no amount
steps.personResponsible: Administrative Aide IV and job order personnel

steps.agency: Unclaimed dogs are rehabilitated with the necessary medication, deworming and vaccination, and put up for adoption.

steps.client: Prospective owners attend an orientation and sign the adoption contract.
steps.agency: Runs the orientation and takes the signed adoption contract.
Dogs with infectious diseases, or in a condition deemed not rehabilitatable, are humanely euthanized.

notes: If your pet has been impounded, you have three days at the barangay facility before it is moved to Banquerohan. Claiming it means paying at the City Treasurer's Office.
Unclaimed animals are rehabilitated and offered for adoption where they can be; those too sick to recover are humanely euthanized.
verifyNotes: The charter prints no TOTAL row, so the total shown is summed from the steps alone.

The charter numbers the first agency action of this service 2.1 rather than 1.1, and the citation ticket row reads only "days from the impounding day" with no number. That step is recorded without a duration.
The charter does not publish the amount an owner pays to reclaim an impounded animal. The step says where it is paid, not how much.
